function.name: requests_get
function.description: Sends a GET request to the specified URL to retrieve weather data from the Open-Meteo API. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

url.description: URL of the Open-Meteo API endpoint.

headers.description: Headers to include in the request. Each key-value pair represents a header field and its value.

Content-Type.description: The MIME type of the body of the request (used with POST and PUT requests).

Accept.description: Media type(s) that is/are acceptable for the response.

timeout.description: Maximum time in seconds to wait for the server to send data before giving up. This is a float type value.

params.description: Query parameters for the GET request.

latitude.description: Latitude of the location, positive for N and negative for S. This is a float type value.

longitude.description: Longitude of the location, positive for E and negative for W. This is a float type value.

elevation.description: Elevation in meters above sea level for the location. The default value represents no elevation downscaling.

auth.description: Authentication tuple for HTTP authentication, in the format (username, password).

cert.description: Path to the SSL client certificate file (.pem). A null value means no client certificate is used.

cookies.description: Dictionary of cookies to send with the request. Each key represents a cookie name.

proxies.description: Dictionary mapping protocol names to the URL of the proxy. Each key-value pair represents a protocol and its proxy URL.

stream.description: If True, the response should be streamed; otherwise, it should be downloaded immediately.

verify.description: Whether to verify the server's TLS certificate.

message.content:
**Artificial Intelligence (AI)** is the field of computer science that focuses on creating systems capable of performing tasks that normally require human intelligence. These tasks include:

| Task | Typical Human Skill | AI Approach |
|------|---------------------|-------------|
| Recognizing speech | Listening & interpreting | Speech‑to‑text models (e.g., Whisper, Whisper‑Large) |
| Understanding language | Reading & reasoning | Natural‑Language‑Processing (NLP) models (e.g., GPT‑4, BERT) |
| Seeing & interpreting images | Visual perception | Computer‑vision models (e.g., CNNs, Vision Transformers) |
| Making decisions | Judgement & planning | Reinforcement learning, rule‑based systems |
| Learning from data | Curiosity & adaptation | Machine‑learning algorithms (supervised, unsupervised, semi‑supervised) |

---

### Core Concepts

| Concept | What it means | Example |
|---------|---------------|---------|
| **Machine Learning (ML)** | Algorithms that improve automatically through experience | A spam filter that learns from new emails |
| **Deep Learning** | ML that uses neural networks with many layers | Image classification with ResNet |
| **Neural Networks** | Computational models inspired by the brain’s neurons | Feed‑forward, recurrent, transformer networks |
| **Training Data** | Labeled examples used to teach a model | Thousands of labeled images for object detection |
| **Inference** | Using a trained model to make predictions | A chatbot answering a user’s question |

---

### Types of AI

| Type | Description | Typical Use‑Case |
|------|-------------|-----------------|
| **Narrow (Weak) AI** | Designed for a single task | Voice assistants, recommendation engines |
| **General (Strong) AI** | Capable of any intellectual task a human can do | Still theoretical; no fully realized system |
| **Super‑AI** | Surpasses human intelligence in all domains | Speculative future scenario |

---

### Historical Milestones

| Year | Milestone | Impact |
|------|-----------|--------|
| 1950 | Turing Test proposed | Set a benchmark for machine “intelligence” |
| 1956 | Dartmouth Conference | Birth of AI as a discipline |
| 1997 | IBM Deep Blue beats Kasparov | Demonstrated machine superiority in a complex game |
| 2012 | AlexNet wins ImageNet | Sparked deep‑learning boom |
| 2020 | GPT‑3 released | Showed large‑scale language modeling |
| 2023 | GPT‑4 & Claude 3 | Advanced reasoning, multimodal capabilities |

---

### Current State & Trends

| Trend | What it means | Why it matters |
|-------|---------------|----------------|
| **Large Language Models (LLMs)** | Models with billions of parameters that can generate text, code, and more | Enable chatbots, content creation, coding assistants |
| **Multimodal AI** | Models that process text, images, audio, and video together | Power tools like DALL‑E, Stable Diffusion, and multimodal chat |
| **AI in Healthcare** | Predictive diagnostics, drug discovery | Improves patient outcomes and speeds research |
| **AI Ethics & Governance** | Fairness, transparency, accountability | Ensures responsible deployment |
| **Edge AI** | Running AI models on devices (phones, IoT) | Reduces latency, preserves privacy |

---

### Common Misconceptions

| Myth | Reality |
|------|---------|
| AI can “think” like humans | AI lacks consciousness; it follows programmed rules and learned patterns |
| AI will replace all jobs | Many roles will evolve; AI augments rather than fully replaces human work |
| AI is always accurate | Models can be biased, overfit, or misinterpret data |

---

### Quick Glossary

- **Algorithm** – Step‑by‑step procedure for solving a problem.
- **Dataset** – Collection of data used for training or testing.
- **Overfitting** – Model performs well on training data but poorly on new data.
- **Bias** – Systematic error that skews results.
- **Explainability** – Ability to interpret why a model made a decision.

---

### Bottom Line

Artificial Intelligence is a rapidly evolving field that builds systems capable of learning, reasoning, and acting in ways that mimic human intelligence. While narrow AI already powers everyday tools—from search engines to autonomous vehicles—research continues toward more general, adaptable, and ethically aligned systems.
